newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SKI FLYING-JAPAN'S OKABE TAKES LEAD AT WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SKI FLYING-JAPAN'S OKABE TAKES LEAD AT WORLD CUP.

text.p: Japan's Takanobu Okabe took the lead on Saturday at a World Cup ski flying competition to set up an exciting duel with local favourite Andreas Goldberger, who came in second after the first jump.

Okabe, who in training flew to a new record on the famous Kulm -- the world's largest natural ski jump -- with a jump of 205 metres earlier in the day, secured the top place with 190.2 points after a first jump of 198.5 metres.
Austria's Goldberger, who last year won his first world championship title on the Kulm, kept his hopes alive with a jump of 191.5 metres to leave him trailing Okabe by just 4.9 points.

Slovenia's Robert Meglic was a surprise third, out-jumping his more celebrated compatriot and current world cup leader Primoz Peterka with a jump of 183.5 metres to go into the second jump on a score of 174.7 points.
The 17-year old Peterka, making his debut on the sunny but gusty Kulm, stood in fifth place behind Kazuyoshi Funaki of Japan.
The final jump is scheduled to take place on Sunday.
